overall: Board did not violate the OML by entering executive session for litigation (Purpose 3) on Nov. 22, 2011, but the notice and the pre-session statement of purpose were insufficient; no remedy ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board's Nov. 22, 2011 executive session for a 'litigation update' was improper because no litigation was pending or threatened over a vacation overpayment.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session at the November 22, 2011 meeting.

allegations.summary: Board's revised motion cited Purpose 7 (privacy statute, G.L. c. 214, sec. 1B) to enter executive session; AG reviewed whether that citation was proper.
allegations.key_passage: The Board also appropriately employed Executive Session Purpose 7 in its revised motion to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: Notice listed only 'Litigation Update' for executive session; AG found it was not specific enough, though the complaint did not raise this issue.
allegations.key_passage: the notice for the Board's November 22, 2011 meeting was not sufficiently specific to advise the public of the topics the Board planned to discuss in executive session.

allegations.summary: Chair's statement of purpose before entering executive session did not cite a valid enumerated purpose or identify the subject matter; AG reviewed this as an additional issue.
allegations.key_passage: the Board's statement of purpose for entering executive session during the November 22, 2011 meeting was also insufficient
